card: Restricts periodic wallet transaction rebroadcasting to only announce transactions to peers if they were missing from the mempool and successfully re-added. Previously, unconfirmed transactions were unconditionally rebroadcast to peers that had not yet seen an inv, even when already present in the local mempool, leaking transaction ownership and node IP. Addresses privacy leak concerns raised in issue #36403.
evidence: PR description references issue #36403 ('Rethinking Transaction Rebroadcasting') and #3828: 'one of the issues with current rebroadcast behavior is that the rebroadcast begins an unconditional relay of a transaction to peers... there is still a privacy leak in this double relay of a transaction, especially so for transactions that are still in nodes' mempools.'
problem: Periodic wallet rebroadcasts unconditionally announce unconfirmed transactions to any connected peers that have not yet received an inventory for them, even if the transaction has resided continuously in the node's mempool. This redundant relay signals to peers that the node has a special interest in the transaction, leaking the user's IP and wallet ownership.

risk.why: A flaw in mempool detection or broadcast mode handling could prevent dropped wallet transactions from rebroadcasting to peers, leaving them unconfirmed until manual user intervention.

scope_notes: Most of the diff (+141/-63) is in `test/functional/wallet_resendwallettransactions.py`, refactoring a single procedural test into isolated helper methods and adding test coverage for load-time resubmissions and rebroadcast suppression.
summary: Adds a new broadcast mode, MEMPOOL_AND_BROADCAST_ADDED, to node transaction broadcast handling and switches periodic wallet rebroadcasts to use it. Transactions already present in the local mempool are retained without being rebroadcast to peers, while transactions that had dropped out and were re-added to the mempool are broadcast. The wallet resend functional test suite is refactored into isolated test methods and expanded to cover mempool-present rebroadcast suppression and wallet-load resubmission.
